content.title: About
content.content: Fine semolina is a high‑quality wheat flour obtained from selected wheat varieties. It has a delicate flavor, soft texture, and a light golden color. Ideal for porridges, doughs, breading mixes, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Semolina is produced from the endosperm of wheat after removing the bran and germ.
Fine semolina absorbs liquid quickly, making it popular in baby foods.
In many cultures semolina is a traditional ingredient for festive dishes such as kutya.
The fine texture allows for smoother batters and creams.
Semolina is carbohydrate‑rich but can fit into a balanced diet when used appropriately.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Its rich carbohydrate content provides a quick source of energy, especially useful for children and athletes.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Contains plant fiber that promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Mineral supply
items.content: Semolina supplies iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, essential for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Compared with some other flours, semolina has a low fat content, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten or wheat allergy may experience reactions after consuming semolina.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Semolina can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Semolina is used to make porridges, couscous, breading mixes, pancake batter, and baked goods. It can be added to soups for thickening or to desserts for a smooth texture. Sifting before cooking helps remove lumps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store semolina in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent pests and spoilage.
